items.text: every sound you leave on the pad carries its name on a tab (bigger while you drag it or hover it), the sound under your finger names itself where it plays, a tap plays a left sound once, and a double-tap opens its halo: which sound, how often, its level, play, take it off
on the screen part, the Room shelf has Clean screen (full screen, every control hidden, nothing reloads) beside Clean output (the stage in its own window)
Board in the Room shelf starts your part's player view, sound only (without a part it opens the Ensemble section to choose one)
water collects where it falls: rain from your finger pools there and runs only to the hollows nearby, never across the floor; the floor is full when most of it holds water
the Corners map: a sound in each corner of the pad and the bed in the middle; while you touch they all play, each as loud as your finger is near it (choose which sound sits in which corner)
Field (or F) shows the field behind the see-through pad, the labels and panels kept, and your finger moves it; Field again is sound only
each of a part's sounds has its own color on the player's pad and in the mixer, and a sound left on the pad shows its name (the screen keeps the part's color)
in Pro, Performing, the Performance board and Clean output each have a switch that turns them on and off right there, saying what they are now (the board says when the screen is too narrow)
Exit leaves the player view, up by the part's name, apart from the panels; tap the part's name on the field to come back

the ensemble's Player view: a part's player sees no field, only the sound: a 16:9 pad the shape of the screen's picture (where you touch here is where your sound lands there), and of the bar only sound, keys and full screen
a mixer of the part's voices: level, timbre, grain and pitch for each, and what plays it (tap, drag, hold, the whole touch, or off); the part's level, bed and mute; reset the part
the pad's map: up and across can play pitch, wetness, grain, timbre, pan or size, over a range you set; four maps to start from (Water, Grain, Timbre, Stage)

the pad is a Cartesian plane: two axes through the middle, A at the top and B at the bottom, C at the left and D at the right, E F H G in the corners; it can stand for a wall, a stage or a floor (the ends are named for it), with zero at the edge or in the middle
leave a sound on the pad: it plays there by itself on the room's beat, every 1, 2, 4 or 8 beats (tap it to change, hold it or drag it off to take it away)
keys for the part: 1 to 5 play its sounds, Space holds, arrows move, Z and X an octave, M mute, [ ] level, D leaves a sound, R Ready to perform, ? the list
on the screen, every sound a player plays lands as a ripple and a ring in the part's color where it was played
a drop that touches a pool joins it, and water meets water in a smooth bridge, never two edges side by side
the Ensemble section in the index folds shut when you tap its title, like every other section
scene pictures fill their rounded frames: no dark, crunchy edge around them
iPhone, iPad and Mac also on the cover, under the paths bar
the rain fill is drawn finer: puddle rims are clean, smooth lines instead of steps and dots
a shelf's title is never cut short: a sequence shows SEQUENCE over its name
the Founders Club says it to you: you keep Pro free, and at 100 Club members get the pre-release of Pro
under the name in the index, what Current is made for: iPhone, iPad and Mac

in the Ensemble the screen leads the room: the scene it shows, picked by hand or played by the robot or a sequence, lands on every player's screen, so everyone sees the same field and each player sees their own touch and plays their own sound; players never take the lead themselves

Ensemble: five players, one piece of water. Each laptop plays one part through its own speaker: Deep (low bubbles, a whale, the hydrophone), Surface (drops, small bubbles, lapping), Shore (gulls, a wave washing up, a lighthouse's low pulse once a bar, surf), Walker (steps on the beat, crunchy sand on the dry side and wading on the wet, splashes) and Beachcomber (a crystal goblet, a bottle blown that follows your finger, a wet finger round a glass rim, a low ringing note). Tap, drag and hold each play a sound of the part; up is higher, right is wetter
a part's link opens Current with that part and joins one room, so the parts share a tempo; the screen's link shows every player's finger on one field, in its part's color, for a projector

Ready to perform, one button in Ensemble and in Room: the paths, hints and notices go quiet, the screen stays awake and nothing reloads; on the screen it also hides every control and goes full screen, a clean picture for the projector (or open the projector window for a second display). Tap again and everything is back as it was
the water surface is drawn finer: small splashes ring round instead of in squares
six water sounds: a step on sand, wading, a splash, a lap, a wave washing up, a lighthouse's turn; and a bottle you blow for as long as you hold
